Author: Nagesh Bheemapaka
Bench: Nagesh Bheemapaka
 1
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka
 Writ Petition No.2314 of 2014
Order:

This writ petition is filed seeking a Writ of Mandamus, declaring the action of the respondent No.2 to recover the compensation amount awarded by the MACT Cum X Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad in M.V.O.P.No.744 of 2012 vide Notice No.01/785(01)/14/- YGT dated 15.01.2014 from the hire bills payable to the petitioner for the bus bearing No. AP 24 X 1604 as illegal and arbitrary and consequently set aside the impugned notice.

entities.text: MACT Cum X Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri D.V. ChalapathiRao, learned counsel for the petitioner; and Sri GaddamSrinivas,
learned Standing Counsel for the respondent- Corporation.
3.

The case of the petitioner, in brief, as per the averments in the writ affidavit, is that the pursuant to the tender notification issued by the respondent Corporation in the year 2008 for supply of passenger bus, one Smt. Y. LaxmiSrinivas had submitted tender notification and stood successful bidder for supply of passenger bus and entered into an Agreement with the 2nd respondent one behalf of 1st respondent Corporation vide Agreement dated 22.02.2008 and started operating the bus bearing No.AP 24X 1604 under hire terms with the respondent Corporation.

It is the case of petitioner that the said Y. LaxmiSrinivas, due to financial conditions, could not continue with the operation of the said bus and offered to sell the bus and the petitioner having agreed to the said offer obtained a No Objection Certificate for transfer of ownership vide Order dated 10.07.2013 from the 2nd respondent and accordingly purchased the bus and operating the bus under the hire terms as per Office Order dated 10.07.2013 by entering into a fresh agreement which is co-terminous with the original agreement entered into with the original bidder.

It is the case of the petitioner that the bus was insured with New India Assurance Company, covering all third party liabilities in the event of any liability arising during the course of operating the bus with the respondent Corporation.

While so, during the course of operation of said bus for the respondent Corporation by its erstwhile owner Y. LaxmiSrinivas, the bus met with an accident on 05.01.2011 resulting in injuries to one B. Shiva Kumar.

The said Shiva Kumar filed a petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- and the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.20,500/- to the P.Yadamma, W/O. Pandu Reddy vs The Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65822287/
1 claimant vide Decree dated 12.06.2013 against the respondent Corporation.
While so, the 2nd respondent issued the impugned Notice dated 15.01.2014 advising the petitioner to deposit the award amount of Rs.20,500/- with costs and interest, totaling to Rs.25,755/-.
Hence, the writ petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the petitioner is operating the bus since 10.07.2013 as per the hire terms and entering into a fresh agreement which is co-terminous with the original agreement, and a No Objection was also issued by the 2nd respondent on 10.07.2013 for transfer of ownership.

It is also contended that the bus is insured with New India Assurance Company and the insurance policy is valid from 23.07.2013 to 04.07.2014, and that the respondent Corporation has not brought the facts about the ownership and the insurance coverage of the bus before the Tribunal while contesting the claim petition filed by the injured B. Shiva Kumar.
Learned counsel contends that the impugned notice seeking to recover the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from the hire bills of the petitioner is illegal and arbitrary.

5. Learned Standing Counsel would contend that as per paragraph 5(iii) of the terms of hire agreement the Corporation shall not be responsible for any damage or loss caused to the vehicle hire during theperiod of agitations, accidents etc., and as per paragraph 5(iv), the owner shall be liable for all claims that may arise due to statutory violations out of the operations , like claims due to accidents payable under theprovisions of M.V. Act, 1988/ Rules and the corporation shall under no circumstances be made liable or responsible to pay compensation that may be awarded by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal or Tribunals in respect of accidents, and therefore there is no illegality in the impugned notice directing the petitioner to deposit the compensation amount of Rs.20,500/-
together with costs and interest awarded by the Tribunal and in there is no illegality in appropriating the amount from the hire bills of the petitioner, and therefore prays that there is no merit in the writ petition.

6. Having considered the respective submissions, and on perusing the material on record, it is pertinent to note that admittedly the petitioner was issued a No Objection Certificate for transfer of ownership of the bus in question vide Office order dated 10.07.2013 and an agreement was entered into between the petitioner and the respondent Corporation from 23.07.2013 to 13.06.2014 which is the 6th year extended period, and the insurance policy was also issued by New India Assurance Company Limited from 23.07.2013 to 04.07.2014 in favour of the petitioner.

Further, it is not in dispute that the petitioner has addressed a letter dated 06.01.2014 bringing to the notice of the respondent Corporation that as on the date of accident the petitioner was not the owner of the bus bearing No.AP 24X 1604 and that the previous owner LaxmiSrinivas has given an affidavit in the Regional Manager office-2nd respondent that she would take the responsibility if any recovered is occurred in respect of the said bus, and that the petitioner purchased the bus on 23.07.2013.

Further it is pertinent to note that the date of issuance of No Objection Certificate dated 10.07.2013 permitting transfer of ownership in favour of petitioner, the accident had already occurred on 05.01.2011 and the claim petition was being contested before the Tribunal and an Award came to be passed on 13.07.2013 for Rs.20,500/- in favour of the claimant against the respondent Corporation.
Further, there is nothing placed on record that there is no valid insurance coverage during the issuance of No Objection certificate by the respondent Corporation for transfer of ownership.

sentences.text:
Further, as per paragraph No.5(iii) of the hire agreement, the owner shall keep the vehicle duly insured comprehensively duly incorporating the Corporation as the hirer of the vehicle in the insurance policy against the Column "Owner" to cover all risks and the proposal form shall be signed by both the owner and the hirer, and in the insurance policy filed by the petitioner, the insurance coverage is shown from 23.07.2013 onwards which is the date of agreement entered between the petitioner and the respondent Corporation and the agreement is the extension of 6th year period,
and further the policy shows the respondent Corporation against the Name of Financier under the Policy Details Column.

Further, as per paragraph 6(iii) of the terms of hire Agreement, the respondent Corporation shall reimburse the owner the Motor Vehicle Tax and Insurance paid by him/her in respect of the operation carried out once in a 15 days in proportionate rate.

It is pertinent to note that there is nothing placed on record that the respondent Corporation has not paid or denied payment of proportionate insurance amount for the relevant period at the time of accident on 05.01.2011 owing to non-existence of insurance coverage.

In that view of the matter, it cannot be said that there is no valid insurance coverage by the date of accident on 05.01.2011 and it cannot be said that the respondent Corporation permitted the petitioner to operate the bus without valid insurance coverage.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation v. Kulsum 1, held as under:
"45.

entities.text: Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation v. Kulsum 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, looking to the matter from every angle, we are of the considered opinion that Insurance Company cannot escape its liability of payment of compensation to Third Parties orClaimants.
Admittedly, owner of the vehicle has not violated any of the terms and conditions of the policy or provisions of the Act.
The owner had taken the insurance so as to meet such type of liability which may arise on account of use of the vehicle."

7. It is pertinent to note that it is not the case of respondent- Corporation before the Tribunal that there was no valid insurance coverage as on the date of accident i.e., 05.01.2011, and that there is lapse on the part of the owner in obtaining the insurance policy, or that the respondent Corporation has stopped paying the proportionate insurance during operation of the bus during 05.01.2011 due to lack of Civil Appeal No.5901 of 2011 :: AIRONLINE 2011 SC 451 insurance coverage or that the owner had not complied with the statutory laws for operating/plying the bus, which goes to show that the bus was being operated as per the terms of hire agreement which mandates following of the statutory laws of paying motor vehicle tax and insurance policy by the owner of the bus.
8.

In that view of the matter, the respondent Corporation is at liberty to proceed against the insurance company for satisfying the Award passed by the Tribunal; and in view of the judgment rendered in Kulsum (1 supra), the insurance company cannot escape its liability to indemnify the insured/petitioner against any claim arising out of operating the vehicle during the valid insurance coverage period.
Therefore the impugned notice of the respondent-Corporation to recover the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from the bills payable to the petitioner is illegal and liable to be set aside.
9. Accordingly the writ petition is allowed, setting aside the impugned Notice No.01/785(1)/14-YGT dated 15.01.2014.
No costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
